title: PhantomEnvironments: Training LLM Agents in Fictional Worlds
data_curation: All training data is rule-generated with no humans or LLMs, at zero marginal cost. The PhantomWiki generator builds a fictional universe of 1,000 people in 100 family trees (easy-mode relations: friendship and immediate family) and renders each person as a templated article that becomes a search document. Multi-hop questions come from context-free grammars (CFG depth 16, up to 7 linear hops), and gold answers come from executing the attached Prolog query, so a question may have multiple answers. Aggregation ('how many') questions are removed because they are easy to reward-hack. A new bidirectional anchor sampler removes the bias toward peripheral answer entities. This yields ~55K training and 5K validation questions. The real-data baseline is a 55K subsample of Search-R1's ~160K NQ+HotpotQA questions on the Wikipedia-2018 corpus.
curriculum: Not a focus of this paper. Every model is RL-fine-tuned in a single stage for 1 epoch directly from the instruct checkpoint (each question seen once). The only scheduling is cell-balanced sampling in the ablation environments: questions are downsampled per (hops, constraints) or (hops, kind) cell, giving 50/50 mixes of pure-hop vs constraint or comparison questions.
method: PhantomEnvironments turns PhantomWiki into an interactive multi-turn search environment: a flat FAISS dense index (e5-base-v2, top-3 docs) over the fictional articles, used through Search-R1-style <search>/<information>/<answer> tags. Training uses GRPO via SkyRL with G=8 rollouts, a token-level F1 reward (SQuAD normalization; equals EM for single answers), retrieved tokens masked from the loss, token-level clip-high at 2.0, no KL penalty, AdamW lr 1e-6 with 10% warmup, 256 prompts per batch, at most 10 turns of 500 tokens, fp32 FSDP2 with vLLM rollouts, and 2 B200s for up to 2 days per run. Models: Qwen2.5-3B/7B-Instruct, Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, Phi-4-mini-instruct, each with 2 seeds. Complexity ablations compare Hops, Hops+Comparisons (age comparisons), and Hops+Constraints (up to 3 attribute filters).
eval_metrics: Token-level F1 on six real-world multi-hop search benchmarks, each with its own corpus: HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue, SynthWorlds-RM, SynthWorlds-SM (500 questions each) and FRAMES (all 824). CofCA is added for the ablations. Evaluation uses a stronger setup than training: Qwen3-Embedding-4B, 20 turns, 32,768 context. Other measures: the Knowledge Advantage gap (SynthWorlds-RM minus SM), a pooled noisy corpus, unseen 1K/10K universes, search calls vs hop count, and knowledge retention (PopQA, MMLU, Wiki-18 perplexity). Example: Qwen2.5-7B FRAMES F1 rises 16.2 -> 35.4 and SynthWorlds-SM 15.6 -> 40.6.
key_results: RL in fictional worlds improves F1 for all four models, averaging 1.7x on the Wikipedia-2018 benchmarks and 2.2x on the newer SynthWorlds/FRAMES benchmarks (Llama-3.2-3B up to 7.1x on SynthWorlds-SM). Real NQ+HotpotQA training wins in-domain (Qwen2.5-3B 56.7 vs 52.2 average F1), but PhantomEnvs wins out-of-domain (32.1 vs 28.4) and closes Qwen2.5-3B's Knowledge Advantage gap from 8% (11% after real-data training) to 0%.
evolution_note: The paper builds on the Search-R1 recipe and PhantomWiki's rule-generated fictional evaluation worlds, extending earlier in-context synthetic-reasoning work to the harder agentic setting where documents must be found by search. It reacts to LLM-synthesized agent environments (ZeroSearch, ASearcher, WebSailor, SWiRL), which risk hallucinated rewards, contamination and API cost, and offers exactly verifiable, LLM-free environments that never go stale. Its finding that linear hops drive transfer while attribute constraints reward a verbatim-query shortcut gives guidance for composing environment complexity axes.
